rows: The hail was reported to be covering the ground.
Numerous cottonwood trees of substantial size were reported damaged on ranch property.
A wood frame barn seven feet tall...fifty feet long...and twenty feet wide was moved twenty feet by the high winds. The barn crushed two horse trailers...a small grain silo and a chain link fence.
Hail occurred on the west side of town.
Sheriff dispatch reported damage to the fire house and other buildings.
At least eight irrigation pivots were damaged by the high winds. No injuries were reported.
A five hundred gallon cattle feeder was blown over and pushed uphill fifty feet.

This tornado formed about two miles south of Wayside in Armstrong county at 1945 CST. Power poles were reported to be damaged and the public reported seeing the tornado drop into Palo Duro Canyon. No injuries were reported.
Hail reported to be three inches deep.

This tornado formed in extreme northeast Armstrong county at 2040 CST and remained over open country. No damage or injuries were reported.
Reported at County Road 1 and Farm to Market Road 1258.
Reported at the intersection of County Road 1 and Farm to Market Road 1258.
The roof was reported blown off of a barn with additional tree and shingle damage in the town of Washburn. No injuries were reported.
Reported on U.S. Highway 287 about one mile inside the Armstrong County line.
Reported seven miles east northeast of Palo Duro Canyon State Park.
The strong thunderstorm wind gusts broke off eight inch diameter tree limbs.

Photographic evidence supported a landspout tornado in Claude. The tornado destroyed a carport and snapped an eight inch diameter tree two feet above the ground. Also...house windows were blown out. The tornado path length and path width were estimated.
The public reported that the thunderstorm wind gust lifted shingles off the roof of a home.
The public reported that the large hail broke the windshield on a vehicle and also broke a window of a home.
The public reported the hail at the Hidden Falls Church Camp at the rim of Palo Duro Canyon.
The public estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts just northwest of Wayside.

A National Weather Service employee estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of sixty-one knots in Claude.
Ham Radio Operator and trained spotter reported the hail near U.S. Highway 287 and Farm to Market Road 2373.

A 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust was estimated by law enforcement officers in Claude.

A member of the public reported quarter size hail 10 miles southwest of Claude.

Late report. Half Dollar size hail reported.
Just east of Claude on hwy 287 a couple of semi-trucks had jackknifed due to strong winds from a thunderstorm.
Golf ball up to tennis ball size hail on Highway 287 east of Goodnight resulted in a cracked windshield.
Hail from dimes to quarters reported, accumulating up to an inch deep in spots.

Chaser reported landspout with corresponding video.
Late report of quarter size hail.

Late report from social media, of wooden structures being blown over and damaged.

Winds stayed above 58 MPH for 5 minutes from 1421 to 1426. The peak gust of 83 MPH occurred at 1422.
Quarter size hail fell 3 miles east-southeast of Washburn.
The West Texas Mesonet station 12 miles southwest of Claude measured gusts in the 63 to 68 MPH range during this time period. The highest gust of 68 MPH occurred at 20:15.
This gust was measured at the JA Ranch West Texas Mesonet station located 4 miles east of Palo Duro.
The JA Ranch West Texas Mesonet station located 4 miles east of Palo Duro measured gusts in the 59 to 66 MPH range. The highest gust of 66 MPH occurred at 1555CST.

A severe thunderstorm dropped large hail from penny size to golf ball size hail across the city of Claude.
The track of this tornado is not accessible by road, but was noted on radar and documented by storm chasers in the area.
A roof was taken off of a front porch. Also a heavy duty swing-set was blown over and several tree limbs were blown down.
Reported mostly quarter size hail with a few stones as large as golf balls. It was also said that a cotton field two miles to the west was completely destroyed.

Multiple reports of 1 to 1.25 in diameter were received between 1918 CDT and 1926 CDT across portions of southwest Amarillo. Some of these reports came in from NWS employees and some came from the public.
Several reports from a storm chaser came in for hail between 1 and 1.75 in diameter along HWY 207 south of Claude.
From the station located SE of Claude.
Mesonet station located SE of Claude.
First wind gust was 58 mph at 1817CDT. Peak wind gust of 71 mph was measured at 1825CDT. Last severe wind gust of 65 mph was measured at 1831CDT.
The sizes of hail reported were between 1.5 and 2.75 in diameter.
This tornado was viewed by storm spotters and captured on video footage. However, it did not produce damage and was generally in an open field.

Large hail fell for about 15 minutes at an outdoor adventure park on the north rim of the canyon with the largest hail up to around ping pong size. At least 3 RVs were damaged and had skylights broken out. Porta potties were also blown about 40 feet from the thunderstorm winds.
A photo of a land spout was submitted via | social media. No damage was reported.

A supercell thunderstorm slowly moved through and south of Claude. It produced a swath of hail ranging from quarter size to grapefruit size. The largest hailstones that measured 3.5 inches and 4.25 inches occurred around ten miles south of Claude.
The mesonet station located 15 miles west southwest of Clarendon gusted to 65 mph at 1640CDT and continued to gust above 58 mph until 1646CDT. The peak gust of 83 mph occurred at 1642CDT.
A truck and camper flipped over on US 287 a mile east of Washburn.

A peak wind gust of 64mph was measured at the mesonet site located ten miles east-northeast of Palo Duro Canyon. This occurred at 901pm. The first severe wind gust of 60mph was measured at 8:58pm and the last severe wind gust of 59mph was measured at 9:03pm.
